summary_html: Agency chooses **Differential Response (DR)**/**Alternative Response**: engage **services without court petition** when safety permits. FFPSA and IV-B/IV-E prevention funding support voluntary, front-end help to avert removals.
authority_html:
- **Family First Prevention Services Act (FFPSA)** — prevention services framework under IV-E  
- **SSA Title IV-B & IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 620–629m; 670–679c)** — service funding & case-plan requirements  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — assesses safety/permanency outcomes in DR systems

District of Columbia - D.C. Code Title 16, Chapter 23, Subchapter I (Proceedings Regarding Delinquency, Neglect, or Need of Supervision)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
key_cases.holding: After trial the court found the District's child welfare system violated federal and District statutory and constitutional requirements at nearly every stage, including a consistent failure to provide services or make reasonable efforts to prevent placement, and ordered systemic relief.
key_cases.relevance: Its findings about the absence of preventive services are the factual baseline against which any District differential-response claim must be measured.
key_cases.quote: the Court finds that defendants have consistently failed to provide services or otherwise use “reasonable efforts” to prevent placement

key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Reasonable efforts require CFSA to identify the barriers to reunification and to refer the parent to appropriate services addressing them; CFSA satisfied that duty here and the change of permanency goal from reunification to adoption was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: It explains that the District's obligation is to make services accessible, which is what a non-court service response must also deliver.
key_cases.quote: requires the District to identify the barriers to reunification and prepare a case plan by recommending appropriate services designed to address the needs of each child and family
